alt: Why different activation functions are needed: regression with any real value uses linear activation, yes or no classification uses sigmoid, and several classes use softmax.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: Without an activation function a neuron computes only z equals w transpose x plus b and the model is linear. With an activation phi of z the model becomes non-linear and can learn complex real-world patterns.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: Table of six activation functions with equation, plot and range: binary step {0,1}, sigmoid (0,1), tanh (-1,1), ReLU [0, infinity), leaky ReLU (-infinity, infinity) and softmax (0,1) with sum 1.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: Sigmoid graph: an S-shaped curve from 0 to 1 that passes 0.5 at input 0. A very large negative input gives close to 0, input 0 gives 0.5, a very large positive input gives close to 1. Output range 0 to 1.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: Tanh graph: an S-shaped curve from minus 1 to plus 1 through the point 0,0. A very large negative input gives close to minus 1, 0 gives 0, a very large positive input gives close to plus 1.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: ReLU formula and graph: ReLU of x is max(0, x). If x is greater than 0 the output is x, if x is 0 or less the output is 0. The graph is flat at 0 for negative inputs and rises linearly for positive inputs.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: ReLU example: neuron outputs 8, 3, 0, -2 and -7 become 8, 3, 0, 0 and 0. ReLU removes the negative values and passes the useful information to the next hidden layer.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: Leaky ReLU formula and graph: f of x is x for x greater than 0 and 0.01 times x for x at most 0. Positive inputs stay the same, negative inputs give a small negative value, not zero.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: Leaky ReLU example: neuron outputs 8, 4, 0, -2 and -5 become 8, 4, 0, -0.02 and -0.05. The neuron keeps learning because the negative value is not zero.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: Softmax example: the scores z equal 2, 1, 0 give e to the z equal 7.39, 2.72, 1 with sum 11.11, and softmax gives about 0.67, 0.25 and 0.09, the probabilities of 3 classes.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: How to choose an activation function: binary classification uses sigmoid, multi-class classification uses softmax, regression uses linear, and hidden layers use ReLU or tanh.
author: Deep Learning faculty
